headline: Scientists discover enzyme that could halt fatty liver disease progression
meta_description: Researchers at Cedars-Sinai identified UBE2N enzyme that protects livers from dangerous MASH condition, offering hope for 100 million Americans.
summary_short: An enzyme called UBE2N could prevent fatty liver disease from worsening into a serious condition affecting millions of Americans.
body:
Researchers at Cedars-Sinai have identified a protective enzyme that appears to stop fatty liver disease from progressing into a more dangerous form. The enzyme, called UBE2N, helps liver cells clear away damaged mitochondria and break down fat, potentially preventing the inflammation, scarring, and cell injury associated with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). In a preclinical study published in Nature Metabolism, scientists found that levels of UBE2N decline as the disease advances—and when they restored the enzyme to normal levels in laboratory mice, fat accumulation, inflammation, and scarring all decreased. The findings could eventually lead to new treatments for a condition that affects an estimated 100 million Americans.

Fatty liver disease, now called metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), often progresses silently. Between 20% and 25% of people with the condition develop MASH, the severe form where excess liver fat combines with inflammation and cell damage. Currently, doctors have few options beyond lifestyle changes; there is no cure, and available medications are limited. This research offers a concrete biological target: if doctors can find ways to maintain or restore UBE2N levels, they might prevent that dangerous progression entirely.

"The identification of this enzyme's role in regulating mitochondria in the liver is an important advance," said Dr. Shelly Lu, director of gastroenterology and hepatology at Cedars-Sinai. Future studies will now test whether enhancing this protective pathway can work alongside existing treatments and help identify which patients would benefit most. For millions living with fatty liver disease, this discovery represents a meaningful step toward prevention rather than just managing damage.
quick_facts: UBE2N enzyme protects livers by clearing damaged mitochondria
100 million Americans have fatty liver disease (MASLD)
20–25% of cases progress to serious MASH condition
Restoring enzyme reduced scarring and inflammation in mice
Cedars-Sinai study published in Nature Metabolism, October 2026
